title: Differential sequence of a strict smooth log morphism
statement:
Let $(Z,L)\xrightarrow{c}(W,M)\xrightarrow{g}(S,N)$ be morphisms of fine log schemes on arbitrary schemes, without a Noetherian assumption. Fine log structures and their morphisms mean log structures etale locally associated to a finitely generated integral monoid chart, with the logification and its universal property as in [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening]. Say $c$ is strict if $L$ is the log structure associated to $c^{-1}M\to\mathcal O_Z$.

For any such morphism $v:(U,H)\to(V,F)$, let $\omega_v$ be the sheaf of $\mathcal O_U$-modules generated by $da$ for local functions and $d\log h$ for local log sections, with additivity and the Leibniz rule for $d$, $d\log(hh')=d\log h+d\log h'$, $d\alpha(h)=\alpha(h)d\log h$, and $da=d\log h=0$ for functions and log sections from the base. For an $\mathcal O_W$-module sheaf $H$, write $c^*H=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{c^{-1}\mathcal O_W}c^{-1}H$, using sheaf tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

If $c$ is strict and its underlying scheme map is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the natural sequence
$$0\longrightarrow c^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\iota}\omega_{gc}\xrightarrow{p}\Omega_{Z/W}\longrightarrow0$$
is exact and locally split as a sequence of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules; here $\Omega_{Z/W}$ is the ordinary relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. The map $\iota$ takes $1\otimes da$ to $d(c^\sharp a)$ and $1\otimes d\log m$ to $d\log(c^\flat m)$; $p$ takes $da$ to its ordinary relative differential and takes $d\log(c^\flat m)$ to zero (so on a unit $v$ of $\mathcal O_Z$ it takes $d\log v$ to $v^{-1}dv$). If $c$ is strict and its underlying scheme map is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $\iota:c^*\omega_g\to\omega_{gc}$ is an isomorphism.
